solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very cold, heartless Greek detains religious adherent

indicators.note: to detain is to hold, so the trimmed Greek word holds the next piece inside it
losing its heart means the middle letter of the Greek word is dropped

parts.note: Attic is the Greek dialect of Athens, so it can stand for Greek
RC is short for Roman Catholic, a follower of that church

explanation.surface: A chilly, unfeeling Greek holds a believer captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the central T of ATTIC, leaving ATIC, which then holds RC.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar regions are proverbially freezing, so the adjective for the far north also means extremely chilly.

clue.text: International winter sportsman, topless, that's taken up manual therapy

indicators.note: in a down entry taken up means read from bottom to top
without its top means the first letter goes

parts.note: a skier takes part in a winter sport

explanation.surface: A topless international skier has taken up hands-on therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Reiki is a Japanese healing practice in which the practitioner's hands are laid on or near the patient.

clue.text: Not the first batsman to suffer in present surroundings

indicators.note: the offering word forms the surroundings, enclosing the suffering word

parts.note: to tender is to present or offer
to ail is to suffer illness

explanation.surface: A lower-order batsman suffering in his current setting.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a tail-ender is one of the weak batsmen who come in last.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's tail-enders bat near the end of the order, so they are far from opening the innings.

clue.text: Minor worker raised Scotch, another alcoholic drink

parts.note: a cog in the machine is an insignificant worker

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means read upwards

parts.note: to scotch is to put a stop to, and to can is to stop

explanation.surface: A lowly worker lifts a Scotch and then another drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky, the 'another' drink, but it is the verb meaning stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, a spirit just as Scotch whisky is.

clue.text: Maybe cabbage and bread the above regularly rejected

parts.note: both bread and brass are slang for money

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the picked letters are read backwards
taking letters at regular intervals picks the first, third and fifth letters

parts.note: in this grid the clue above is 1 across, whose answer is the word for very cold

explanation.surface: A cabbage, perhaps, alongside some bread, both turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: In a Telegraph puzzle 'the above' can mean the answer of the clue printed just above, here 1 across; 'regularly' picks its odd letters and 'rejected' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabbage belongs to the brassica genus of plants, so it is one example; 'Maybe' signals that.

clue.text: Team's set on fire part of the match after runs by Boycott

indicators.note: by means beside, so the boycott word sits next to the rest
after says the match part comes after the runs

parts.note: to black a firm is to boycott it
to burn is to set on fire
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
overs are the six-ball units of a cricket match

explanation.surface: A team set alight part of a cricket match after runs by Geoffrey Boycott.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott was a famous England batsman, so 'runs by Boycott' looks like cricket scoring; here Boycott is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an English football club from Lancashire, a sports side.

clue.text: Sound of puff adder's fellow creature, enraged

parts.note: the asp is a snake, like the adder
irate means angry

explanation.surface: A puff adder's companion makes a furious hissing noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puff adder' looks like the African snake, but 'puff' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirate is the breathy H sound, a puff of air in speech.

clue.text: Endless crouching exercise beginning to drain group of soldiers

indicators.note: without its end means the last letter goes

parts.note: a squat is an exercise done by crouching

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Endless squats are starting to wear out the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A squad is a small military unit, a section of soldiers.

clue.text: Noxious Beatnik, without a cent, wearing headphones

indicators.note: the trimmed writer wears the headphones, so goes inside them

parts.note: cans is slang for headphones

indicators.note: without means the following letters are removed

parts.note: Jack Kerouac was the leading Beat Generation writer
a is A and C is the abbreviation for cent

explanation.surface: A noxious, penniless beatnik in headphones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beatnik' looks like any hipster, but here it names the Beat writer himself; 'without' strips the A and C at the end of his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cankerous spreads corruption like a canker, so it is harmful or poisonous.

clue.text: TV sitcom's revolting commercial turned over by house member

parts.note: people revolting are in a rising, an uprising

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so these two letters run backwards

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
an MP is a Member of Parliament, of the House of Commons

explanation.surface: A sitcom's disgusting advert gets overturned by a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising Damp' was a 1970s British sitcom set in a shabby boarding house; 'revolting' looks like 'disgusting' but means rising up.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a well-known British television comedy series starring Leonard Rossiter.

clue.text: Part of arms deal's ending, between global alliance and America

indicators.note: between means the final letter is placed inside the alliance letters, ahead of America

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is a worldwide alliance of states

indicators.note: the ending of the word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An arms deal concludes between the United Nations and the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' suggests weapons, but the definition is anatomical: L, the end of deal, goes between U and N, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the two long bones of the forearm, so it is a part of each arm.

clue.text: Movement of crab perhaps that's followed by Miami pedestrians

definitions.meaning: a crab scuttles sideways, so its gait is a sideways step, read as two words
the American word for pavement, a path walkers in Miami follow

explanation.surface: A crab's sideways scuttle is copied by people walking in Miami.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it describes the crab's gait; as one, it is the US word for the British pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs travel sideways, and the American term for the paved path beside a road is the same letters.

clue.text: Body of water dried up, eastern half first

indicators.note: in an across entry the eastern half is the right-hand half, which is moved to the front

parts.note: seared means scorched and dried up

explanation.surface: A parched sea where the east has dried out first.
explanation.walkthrough: SEARED split in two gives SEA and RED; moving the right-hand half to the front gives RED SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the narrow sea between Africa and the Arabian peninsula, a large body of salt water.

clue.text: Boss's stomach, in the past, heard by some

indicators.note: heard says the word is spoken; by some because only some accents make the two sound alike

parts.note: to stomach is to tolerate or stand, and the past tense of stand is stood

explanation.surface: The boss's stomach of former times, as some heard it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss's stomach' reads as a manager's belly, but 'Boss' is the definition, a raised ornament, and 'stomach' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a knob or raised ornamental stud on a surface such as a shield or ceiling.

clue.text: Changed habit, when obtaining English journal around republic

indicators.note: obtaining means taking in, so the rearranged letters hold the rest
changed means the letters are put in a new order
turned around means read backwards

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a journal

explanation.surface: A changed outfit when an English magazine arrives around a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: HABIT rearranged to THBIA takes in E and GAM.
explanation.definitionFit: This West African state along the river of the same name is a republic.

clue.text: New Wave band playing extra-loud, unconfined, around five

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit around the Roman numeral
playing suggests the letters being played about with into a new order
without its confines means the outer letters of the word are removed

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A New Wave group performing at high volume, letting loose around five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unconfined' strips E and D from EXTRALOUD, leaving XTRALOU; 'playing' rearranges that around V.
explanation.definitionFit: This British synth-pop group, fronted by Midge Ure, was a leading act of the early 1980s New Wave.

clue.text: One describes a policeman, Jack, replacing Ernest on vacation

indicators.note: replacing says the jack letter takes the place of the vacated name

parts.note: a detective is a police officer

indicators.note: vacated, emptied of its middle, leaving the outside letters

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A policeman named Jack stands in for Ernest while he is on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNEST emptied is ET; J replaces ET in A DETECTIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: This part of speech describes a noun, so it is one word that does the describing.

clue.text: Native American without fear, wandering untroubled

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the people surround the rest

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people

indicators.note: wandering letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A fearless Native American roaming, free of worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking', which would delete fear; here it means outside, so the people go round the rearranged fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone free of cares is happy and without worries.

clue.text: Apple and some corn Mike put inside French bread

indicators.note: put inside means the corn and Mike go within the French word

parts.note: pain is the French word for bread
an ear is a head of corn
Mike is M in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: An apple and corn put by Mike into a French loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The Worcester Pearmain is an old English variety of eating apple.

clue.text: Deserved first from schoolteacher in project

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the word for project

parts.note: to project is to jut out

indicators.note: the first letter taken from the following word

explanation.surface: A first-rate mark from a teacher for a school project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' looks like a school assignment, but it is the verb, to stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: A just reward is one that is deserved, so the adjective means fairly earned.

clue.text: Devise another furtive system to find fish in middle of creek

indicators.note: in means the fish goes inside the middle letters
the middle of the word is its letters apart from the outer ones

parts.note: the cod is a fish

explanation.surface: Plot a secret new system to locate fish in a creek.
explanation.walkthrough: A code is a secret system of writing, so 'furtive system'.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a new cipher is to invent a fresh secret system for it.

clue.text: Black fish that circles wrist

definitions.note: the definition is a description, the thing that goes round a wrist

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to fish with rod and line is to angle

explanation.surface: A black fish that coils itself around someone's wrist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigid bracelet worn round the arm or wrist is an item of jewellery that encircles it.

clue.text: Relish Hebridean island, except for current during journey

indicators.note: during means inside the journey

parts.note: to go is to travel, and a go can be a trip

indicators.note: except for means the following letter is left out

parts.note: Uist is an island in the Outer Hebrides, off Scotland
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Enjoying a Hebridean island, except for the tides, on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relish' looks like a verb, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment, the zest of doing something with pleasure.

clue.text: Left shed grey

parts.note: left as in remaining, left over
a snake that sheds its skin casts it

explanation.surface: Someone left a shed painted grey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' and 'shed' look like a departure and a garden hut; both are other senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A sky covered with cloud is dull and gloomy in colour, so the weather word means grey.

clue.text: African extremists infiltrating south Caribbean

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside the Caribbean letters

parts.note: WI is the West Indies, the Caribbean islands
A and Z are the extremes of the alphabet

explanation.surface: African militants are infiltrating the southern Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists' looks like militants, but means the first and last letters of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swazi is a person from Eswatini, formerly Swaziland, in southern Africa.

clue.text: Bird's relative one recalled

indicators.note: called back means the letters run backwards

parts.note: a sib is a sibling, a brother or sister
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bird's relative is remembered by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a downcurved bill, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Inflated the new ball Clair kicked around by river

indicators.note: by means next to, so the river letter sits beside the rest
made new means the three letters are re-formed

parts.note: O is shaped like a ball

indicators.note: the name is kicked around into a different order

explanation.surface: Clair kicks the new ball around beside the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like an adjective for the ball, but it is an anagram signal acting on 'the' alone; the river letter, placed 'by' the rest, leads the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetorical language is high-flown and pompous, so it is bombastic or puffed-up in style.

clue.text: Posh lady's deepish voice — it's gone extremely sensuous

indicators.note: gone means removed from the voice word

parts.note: a baritone is a male voice between tenor and bass, fairly deep
taken as written

indicators.note: the extremes of the word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A grand lady's low voice has lost its sensual quality.
explanation.walkthrough: BARITONE without IT leaves BARONE, followed by S and S, the ends of sensuous.
explanation.definitionFit: A baroness is a woman holding a title in the peerage, an aristocrat.

clue.text: Some of Observer's reporting indeed associated with papers on Left

indicators.note: in an across entry one piece on another sits after it
reporting means the word is spoken out

parts.note: aye means yes, indeed
ID is identity papers

explanation.surface: The Observer newspaper reports on papers linked to the political Left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observer' suggests the newspaper, but it is someone looking; part of their eye is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelid is a fold of skin covering the eye, so it is one part of a person who watches.
